summary.text: Genetics studies genes, the differences between them, and how traits are passed down in living things.
Gregor Mendel, a friar in 19th-century Brno, was the first to study it scientifically, tracing traits from parents to offspring in pea plants.
Modern genetics also studies how genes function and behave, and how they work together with an organism's environment and experiences.

facts.label: Mendel's subject
facts.value: Pea plants, with inheritance patterns described mathematically

facts.label: Rediscovery
facts.value: Mendel's work was widely understood only in 1900, after his death

facts.label: Genes on chromosomes
facts.value: Thomas Hunt Morgan argued this in 1911 using fruit flies

items.prompt: Two corn seeds have identical genes. One is planted in a mild, wet climate and one in a dry climate, and the dry one ends up much shorter. What best explains this?

options.label: The dry plant's genes changed to match the dry soil
Genes only work in mild climates, not dry ones
The environment can limit growth even when genes are the same
Identical seeds always grow to the same height

items.explain: Genes set an average height the plant could reach, but a lack of water and nutrients held the dry plant to half the height.

items.prompt: A 19th-century breeder believes offspring always get a smooth mix of their parents' traits. What did Mendel's pea experiments show against this?

options.label: Traits come from distinct genes in combination, not a continuous blend
Offspring always look exactly like one parent
Traits only change when the plant is moved to a new place
Parents pass on only the traits they have strengthened

items.explain: Mendel found traits were not blended after hybridization, which showed they are produced by combinations of distinct genes.

items.prompt: A weightlifter trains for ten years and builds huge muscles. Based on what is now known, how do those years of training affect the genes passed to her children?

options.label: Her strengthened traits are passed on to her children
Her genes shift a little with each year of training
Her genes change, but only in her sons
They do not change; experiences don't affect inherited genes

items.explain: The idea that individuals inherit traits strengthened by their parents is now known to be wrong, because experiences do not affect the genes passed on.

items.prompt: A researcher in the early 1900s examines a mealworm and finds cells with both an X and a Y chromosome. Going by Nettie Stevens's findings, what sex is it?

options.label: Female
Male
Either one
Neither one

items.explain: Stevens discovered that females had only the X chromosome while males had both X and Y.

items.prompt: In 1911 a scientist argued that genes are located on chromosomes. What observation did he build the argument on?

options.label: Seed shapes handed down in pea plants
Differences in height between dry and wet corn
A white eye mutation in fruit flies that was linked to sex
Sex differences in chromosomes of mealworms

items.explain: Thomas Hunt Morgan based his argument on a sex-linked white eye mutation he observed in fruit flies.

items.prompt: A farmer saves seed only from her biggest squash each year, hoping the next crop will be bigger. What observation is she relying on?

options.label: Living things inherit traits from their parents
A plant's size depends only on its water supply
Seeds change to match what the farmer wants
Traits skip generations at random

items.explain: Since prehistoric times, people have used the fact that living things inherit traits from their parents to improve crops through selective breeding.
